Feature Comparison: Python 3.8 vs Python 3.9

Adoption Stability: Python 3.8.0 was widely adopted and considered highly stable for production. Python 3.9.0 offered more features but required newer library versions, reducing immediate production adoption.

Feature Python 3.8.0 Python 3.9.0
Release Date 2019-10-14 2020-10-05
End of Life 2024-10-07 2025-10-05
Walrus Operator (:=) Supported Supported
Dictionary Merge (|) Not supported Supported
Built-in Type Generics Not supported (use typing module) Supported (list[int], dict[str, int])
zoneinfo Module Not available (use pytz) Supported
str.removeprefix() Not available Supported
Key Features Walrus operator, positional-only params Dict merge, type generics, zoneinfo

Summary

Python 3.9.0 builds on 3.8 by adding dictionary merge operators, built-in type generics, zoneinfo, and string utility methods. Python 3.8 introduced the walrus operator and positional-only parameters.

For production stability in 2019-2020, Python 3.8.0 was preferred due to wider library support and proven reliability. Python 3.9.0 offered more features but required newer library versions for compatibility.
